evidence.detail: space329/ac1/bound-and-plain: the install puts both hooks, executable, in the shared hooks folder of a bound repository and of a plain one; a linked worktree made before the install uses the same folder; git itself then runs them: a worktree add and a trunk commit each start the CLI with the state root and git's own lines.
space329/ac1/configured-folder: with core.hooksPath set by its absolute path in the repository's local configuration the hooks go to that folder, none to the shared one, and git runs them from there.

space329/ac1/keeps-own-lines: two existing shell hooks of the owner's keep every line, in order, and gain one marked line; the owner's lines still run with git's input whole (prepared and committed), Veldo's hook runs beside them with the same input, the temporary folder cannot be written, and a second install changes no byte.

space329/ac1/refused-and-said: a program hook, a link and a hook git does not run are refused by name with why and left byte for byte; an earlier copy of Veldo's own hook is replaced and kept beside it; a file of the owner's under Veldo's name is refused.

space329/wiring/bootstrap-installs: the service's start (bootstrap) installs for the repository bound at that start, the named plain repository and the named account folder, and logs each with the folder used.

assumptions: Criteria remain pending until the lead runs the canonical gate, ./scripts/verify.sh. Neither the full gate, the policy check, nor suites 151, 153, 154 and 155 were run. Suite 156_veldo_0315_reconcile was run in the fix round and passed. The first fix round was re-reviewed (FIX, one finding). The second fix round is not yet reviewed: its review runs in a fresh context.

Binding installs at the service's start: bootstrap reads the bound repositories and calls the installer, so a repository gets its hooks at the first start after it is bound. No bind command outside the footprint was changed. The first start of a real service with space management enabled therefore writes into the hooks folder and git configuration of every bound and named plain repository and into settings.json of every named account folder. Nothing on the protect list is touched, and no live repository or account folder was touched by this build.

The engine finds its hook files in hooks/ beside .veldo (or engine/hooks in this repository) and the session script in packs/claude/scripts beside or above the engine. Whether a deployed engine carries both there was not measured. Where it does not, the install record names the refusal and reconcile reports the hooks as missing; nothing is silent.

Chained hooks are shell hooks only (sh, bash, dash, ksh, zsh by their first line). A program, a link, a file with no first line naming a shell and a hook that is not executable are refused and reported, by the owner's rule that an existing hook is kept and chained or refused. An owner's shell hook that the marked line precedes still receives git's input; where neither the hooks folder nor the temporary folder takes the input copy, the owner's lines run and that landing is left to the next reconcile.

The trunk a hook is told (veldo.space.trunk) is the one the work configuration's land entry gives through the spool's about; the fixture has none, so no row sets it. The client was played by running the installed command through sh; no live client was started.
The reports are findings of the reconcile result (hooks_missing and session_hooks_missing), which the service logs; the space.reports API route belongs to a later ticket.

Fix round, finding 1: the owner's configuration is the one the service's own environment gives git (HOME, and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM when set). An owner whose terminal uses another global file than the service is not seen. A repository under a global hook manager gets no Veldo hook; it is refused and reported at every start until the owner names a folder in the repository's local configuration.

Fix round, finding 2: a relative core.hooksPath and a hooks folder inside a work tree are refused, not served. A repository that keeps its hooks committed gets no Veldo hook and is reported. The check for a work tree or repository above the folder walks the folder's ancestors for a .git entry or a git directory; a fixture or temporary folder that itself lies inside a work tree would be refused the same way.

Fix round, finding 4: refusing was chosen over a second entry. The git hook reads one veldo.space.stateroot, and a session reported to two ledgers would have two owners. The design names no case of two installations for one folder; this is the builder's reading, for the owner to confirm. An installation whose state root moves is reported as another installation until the owner takes the old entries out.

Fix round, finding 5: the client takes no lock, so a client write between the compare and the rename itself (a few system calls) can still be replaced; the lock serializes Veldo installers only, and the read after the rename catches a write that follows. The lock file .settings.json.veldo-lock stays in the account folder.

Fix round, finding 6: the deadline is 10 seconds for each run of a hook, under timeout(1). On a host with no timeout(1) the hook runs without it and the bound is the CLI's own wait (control_space_spool.REACH_SECONDS for each answer); that path was not run. A repository installed before this fix has its marked line rewritten at the next start.

Second fix round, finding 1: the other worktrees' own files are read only when extensions.worktreeConfig is true in the repository's configuration, at reconcile, not at install; a worktree found there is reported and nothing is installed in its folder. A worktree whose folder is gone is left out, and one git could not read is named as unread. The report is one finding for the repository, with the worktrees joined by commas.

Second fix round, included file: a configured hooks folder is taken only where git names the repository's own config file (the common directory's config) as the origin of core.hooksPath. A config file that is itself a link is refused the same way.

Second fix round, timeout -k: the marked lines use timeout -k 2 10. timeout(1) kills what it started, Veldo's hook, when that ignores TERM. Measured by hand in a scratch folder: under the shipped hook, a CLI that ignores TERM is NOT killed. The hook's shell ends at TERM, timeout(1) leaves with it before the kill step, git goes on at the deadline, and the CLI is left running without a parent. Ending such a CLI needs a change in engine/hooks (for one, trap : TERM, so the shell stays until the kill step), which this round did not touch.
rollback: Revert the fix round's commits and the two build commits. Hooks already installed stay where they are and keep working; a repository bound afterwards gets none. The marked lines, Veldo's own files and the lock file beside a settings file can be taken out by hand; nothing of the owner's was changed beyond the one marked line.
